newsitem.title: FRANCE: France welcomes U.S. approval of troops for Zaire.
newsitem.headline: France welcomes U.S. approval of troops for Zaire.

text.p: France welcomed a White House announcement on Wednesday that President Bill Clinton had agreed in principle to order U.S. troops to participate in an international humanitarian mission for Zaire.

"France welcomes this decision, which will enable the force to get off the ground without delay and dispatch humanitarian aid to those people who are in distress," the French Foreign Ministry said in a statement.

France, which has been pushing hard for a multinational force on condition that Washington agreed to contribute soldiers, urged quick United Nations approval so that the mission could begin to help hundreds of thousands of refugees deprived of food and water by fighting in eastern Zaire.

The French statement said that Foreign Minister Herve de Charette would immediately begin to flesh out the details of the operation with U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher, who was in Paris for a conference on Bosnia on Thursday.
It said that de Charette would also be conferring with Canadian Foreign Affairs Minister Lloyd Axworthy.
Canada has agreed to lead the multinational force.
